name: Banner
summary: Prominent message spanning a wide region. variant="consent" is the cookie notice, with the preferences window.

a11y.apg: Same live-region rule as Alert: `danger` is role="alert", the rest role="status". The only focusable thing is the dismiss button, and it appears only when you pass `onDismiss` — reachable by Tab, with an accessible name from the i18n strings. variant="consent" is not a live region: it is role="region" named by its h2, the three buttons are reachable by Tab, the preferences are a Dialog, and after a choice the confirmation (role="alert") receives the focus, because the button that was pressed is gone.

props.name: variant
props.description: Tone, and the same live-region rule as Alert: `danger` is role="alert", the rest role="status". `consent` is the cookie notice: a region named by its h2, the text, and three buttons of the SAME weight — reject the non-essential, accept all, choose — then the confirmation, which takes the focus. Put it at the top of the page, before the skip link, and do not fix it to the screen.

props.name: title
props.description: Rendered as a <strong> above the body. On consent it is the h2 that names the region; without it, the strings' consentTitle.

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph in the leading column. Leave it out and the column still holds its place — an empty span keeps the three-column grid — so banners stacked together stay aligned.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Passing it is what draws the close button. Without it the banner cannot be dismissed, which is the right default for something the reader has to see. On consent it is the "Hide this message" button of the confirmation; without it the notice hides itself.

props.name: state
props.type: waiting_user | waiting_approval | waiting_dependency | offline | stale | partial | degraded
props.description: Universal state (Part J) — same axis and same derivation as on Alert: `variant` is severity, `state` is the condition. It sets `data-state`, picks the severity when no `variant` is given, and supplies the message when there are no children. A banner is the page-width place to say “no connection” or “working with reduced capability”, which is why it carries the same vocabulary as the inline alert instead of a second one.

props.name: categories
props.description: Only on consent: the categories of the preferences window, in order — {id, label, description?, required?}. Required ones are always on and have no switch; the others start OFF.

props.name: value
props.description: Only on consent: the choice already stored, {[id]: boolean}, so the person can come back and change it — show the notice again from a "Cookie settings" link. Without it, only the required categories are on.

props.name: onConsent
props.description: Only on consent: the choice made, for the app to store and obey. Required categories always come as true.
